security_spec.violation_condition: KVM restores a stale hstatus.MTAG_I (from a previous VM exit) that does not match the current trapping instruction's code-page PTE.MTAG, then executes HLV/HSV instructions via kvm_riscv_vcpu_unpriv_read(), causing HLV tag-check policy to diverge from what the guest's native execution would have produced
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csr_write(CSR_HSTATUS, ...) | csr_swap(CSR_HSTATUS, ...) where the written value contains an MTAG_I bit not reflecting the current trap's code page MTAG; csr_write(CSR_MSTATUS, ...) where MTAG_I is clobbered before MPRV loads/stores
security_spec.summary: hstatus.MTAG_I is hardware-deposited on trap entry and controls HLV/HSV tag-check policy; kernel must not clobber it before HLV emulation and must not leak stale values across VM boundaries

findings.finding: csr_swap(CSR_HSTATUS, vcpu->arch.guest_context.hstatus) loads the guest hstatus verbatim, including whatever MTAG_I bits the guest context carries, before executing HLV/HSV instructions. If MTAG support is added in future silicon, this could load a stale MTAG_I from the guest context that diverges from the trapped instruction's code-page PTE.MTAG. Currently safe because the kernel defines no MTAG_I bit and no RISC-V MTE support exists in this tree.

The standard (non-NACL) VCPU entry path does csr_swap(CSR_HSTATUS, gcntx->hstatus), directly loading the full guest hstatus into hardware. Same concern as above: if MTAG_I were defined in future hardware, this path would load an unfiltered MTAG_I that may not match the trap's code-page PTE.MTAG.
kvm_arch_vcpu_load does not write hstatus at all; it only loads vsstatus/vsie/vstvec/henvcfg/hgatp etc. No MPRV or MSTATUS manipulation. No MTAG/MTE-related CSR access. Compliant.
findings.snippet: /* hstatus NOT loaded in vcpu_load path */

findings.finding: kvm_arch_vcpu_put also does not read/write hstatus directly. No MSTATUS or MPRV handling. No tag-related CSR manipulation. Compliant.
findings.snippet: /* hstatus NOT saved in vcpu_put path */

findings.finding: The assembly trap handler invoked on HLV/HSV fault simply saves scause/stval/htval/htinst into the kvm_cpu_trap structure, advances SEPC by 4, and does sret. No CSR manipulation beyond reading trap CSRs. No MTAG-aware logic needed at this level.
findings.snippet: /* saves: scause, stval, htval, htinst; advances SEPC; sret */

findings.finding: Restore path properly writes back old_hstatus and old_stvec via csr_write. The save/restore pair is correctly bracketed by local_irq_save/restore. No window where a corrupt hstatus could leak across contexts.
